# The 1,000 most-committed Claude Code statuslines, one section each

Ranked by commits (a fork counts only the commits it added over its parent). Each section was written by a haiku agent from the project's downloaded source on 2026-10-25; anchors point into that source. How the list was chosen and what the fields mean: [README.md](README.md).

## 1. bllshttng/fno
31995 commits (28016 in the last 90 days), 2 stars, last commit 2026-10-26
- url: https://github.com/bllshttng/fno
- what: statusline inside a larger tool (fno, an autonomous agent-orchestration workflow plugin; the buddy mod at plugins/buddy runs without it)
- size: ~275 statusline code lines (hooks/statusline.py 248, hooks/statusline.sh 25), plus the 1003-line hooks/register.ts mod that feeds it, Python, bash, TypeScript
- shape: rich
- data sources: stdin, transcript, git, github/PRs, claude-config-files, other:fno CLI state, other:model API (haiku calls)
- lineage: credits X as inspiration (Claude Code's original built-in buddy: the code calls it "the original", copies its rarity theme keys from Claude Code 2.1.294 in hooks/companion.ts, and re-creates its card and speech bubble)
- why it exists: revives Claude Code's removed buddy companion beside the status line, published as a standalone mod; the fleet news ties it to the author's fno tool
- beyond baseline: wrapper composes the user's own statusline command with a buddy sprite and speech bubble flushed right (hooks/statusline.py:layout); bash fast path reprints cached output unless input, width or frame changed (hooks/statusline.sh); each turn's speech is a haiku model call, with personality written once at hatch (hooks/register.ts:react, givePersonality); loud turns (test failures, errors, big diffs) skip the quiet gap (hooks/voice.ts:loudReason); idle talk claimed once across sessions every 2 min (hooks/register.ts:claimIdle); fleet line of live workers, open asks and open PRs from fno and gh (hooks/register.ts:readFleet); fno feed news and rerolls earned per shipped PR (hooks/register.ts:readFeed, refill); species, rarity and stats derived from a seed (hooks/companion.ts:hatch); settings.json statusLine rewritten to the wrapper with refreshInterval 1 and a saved copy of the user's line for rollback (hooks/register.ts:statuslineOn, statuslineOff); every line logged to observations.jsonl (hooks/register.ts:remember)
- summary: The buddy is a companion sprite drawn beside the user's own status line, not a statusline of its own: statusline.py runs the user's saved command (inner.json, cached per session) and prints it with the sprite, bubble and fleet line from frame files the mod writes. The mod (hooks/register.ts) runs a 500 ms clock, installs the wrapper into settings.json with refreshInterval 1, and rewrites its frame each tick. Speech is one haiku call per turn, gated by a 30 s gap that loud turns skip, plus an idle line every two minutes. The fleet line and fno feed news draw from `fno agents gate-status`, `fno inbox outstanding`, `gh pr list` and `fno-agents feed`, shared through the mod's store so sessions do not each pay for them. statusline.sh avoids starting Python on ticks where nothing changed.

- shape: rich

## 6. hasuwini77/claude-pulse
5979 commits (2057 in the last 90 days), 1 stars, last commit 2026-09-16
- url: https://github.com/hasuwini77/claude-pulse
- what: config or wrapper for another statusline (wraps ccstatusline 2.2.22 and adds its own usage segment)
- size: ~190 code lines (statusline/statusline.sh 45, statusline/claude-pulse-statusline.js 142; the usage fetcher in core/src is a separate TypeScript package), bash, JavaScript
- shape: rich
- data sources: stdin, usage-api, system, other:ccstatusline
- lineage: wraps or configures ccstatusline (statusline.sh runs the globally installed ccstatusline dist, recolours its Tango ANSI codes to a Catppuccin palette, and ships a ccstatusline settings file)
- why: author's usage HUD, published with a palette; the stock statusline does not show Claude plan windows
- beyond: 5-hour and weekly utilisation with reset countdown and extra-usage credits (statusline/claude-pulse-statusline.js, main); usage read from a snapshot the scheduler writes, with the only fetcher calling the OAuth usage endpoint (CONTRACT.md, core/src/fetcher.ts); self-heal that asks launchd to run the fetch job when the snapshot is over 20 minutes old (kickFetcherIfStale, throttled by a stamp file); thinking-effort segment parsed from stdin in bash (statusline/statusline.sh)
- summary: The statusline is mostly a wrapper: statusline.sh pipes the stdin JSON to ccstatusline, recolours its output to a Catppuccin palette, and appends a usage segment and a thinking-effort segment. The usage segment only reads data/usage.json and never touches the network or the credentials file. That snapshot is written by a separate fetcher run by a platform scheduler (scheduler/install-*.sh) against the OAuth usage endpoint. If the snapshot is over 20 minutes old and the macOS fetch agent is installed, the segment runs launchctl kickstart, at most once per 15 minutes. It prints a red ! when the data is over 30 minutes old or the last fetch failed.

- lineage: none found (upstream of Nishant-Rajj/claude-statusbar, which its own README calls "a hardened local fork" of this project and which copies its code)
- why it exists: Claude Code shows almost nothing about rate-limit headroom, so this puts the 5h and 7d limits, their reset times, end-of-window projections and a prompt-cache countdown on one line (README).
- beyond baseline: end-of-window projection from average pace since the window opened, with an at-risk ETA chip (src/claude_statusbar/predict.py project_window, forecast_chip); per-account quota reconciliation so a replayed older snapshot cannot lower a newer reading (predict.py reconcile_account); prompt-cache countdown from the newest assistant entry in a bounded transcript tail (core.py _last_assistant_info, get_cache_age_text); live todo, running-tool and subagent lines from the same kind of tail (activity.py); opt-in per-model caps from api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage (scoped_usage.py); relay balance for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL relays (core.py relay_balance, _balance_refresh.py); opt-in IP-risk line from external IP-check endpoints (_ip_risk_refresh.py); long-lived daemon that prerenders rendered.ansi on a 1 s tick (daemon.py)
- summary: A thin client prints a prerendered line from rendered.ansi, and daemon.py re-renders that file on a 1 s tick, so each Claude Code tick is mostly a file read (daemon.py docstring). Quota state is shared across sessions for each account and reconciled so an older replayed snapshot cannot overwrite a newer one (predict.py reconcile_account; CHANGELOG v3.52.2). The end-of-window projection uses average pace over the whole elapsed window rather than a recent burst, and a bounded history learns work and off-hour rates (predict.py header). The cache countdown and activity lines both read a bounded reverse tail of the transcript (core.py, activity.py). Relay users get balance and no-quota mode from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and the bearer key, fetched in the background (core.py relay_balance). Updater, IP-check and balance refreshes run as child processes so the render path never blocks on the network (core.py check_for_updates, _ip_risk_refresh.py).

If stdin has no `rate_limits` it falls back to the OAuth usage API, and it flags a 🔥 when the burn rate projects past 100%. ## 379. mpecan/rusted-claude-meter

- size: ~1,500 lines across crates/meter-files/src/statusline (bridge 370, setup 369, freshness 166, appimage 224, mod 212, config 106), src/statusline-setup.ts (57) and src-tauri/src/bin/statusline.rs (4); many are doc comments and tests, and the pace rule is in crates/meter-core/src/snapshot.rs
- shape: rich
- data sources: stdin, transcript, local-history, claude-config-files
- lineage: ports ClaudeMeter (the Swift menu-bar app; CLAUDE.md calls this a port of the SwiftUI ClaudeMeter, and the pace code mirrors its UsageData.paceSignal)
- why it exists: show plan usage in the prompt, from the rate-limit numbers Claude Code already sends, so the app need not poll claude.ai
- beyond baseline: 5h and 7d figures read from the stdin rate_limits object and merged across sessions in ~/.claudemeter/statusline.json, keeping the freshest reading (crates/meter-files/src/statusline/freshness.rs:63 merge); a pace flag: 🔥 when a window burns faster than a sustainable rate, shown only from a 1.2 ratio, and a cold mark when the weekly window is underused (crates/meter-files/src/statusline/bridge.rs:221 pace_segment; crates/meter-core/src/snapshot.rs:126 pace_signal); a /statusline setup route that has the agent edit ~/.claude/settings.json (src/statusline-setup.ts)
- summary: The bridge binary reads Claude Code's status-line JSON from stdin, takes the 5-hour and 7-day used percentages and their reset times, and merges them into a shared file that the menu-bar app also reads. It prints `5h 37% · 7d 61%`, with a pace marker appended when the windows are burning fast or underused. The pace ratio compares used percentage with the share of the window already elapsed over a 5-to-7-day weekly span, so the marker is a rate, not a raw figure. The reading's timestamp comes from the transcript's last modification time, not from the render time, so an idle session does not look fresh. Errors print nothing rather than a broken status line.

The Codex patch is gated by a supported-versions table of exact upstream commits.

When the plugin has written nothing, it falls back to model id, context % and cost from stdin (internal/statusline/statusline.go:223). The status line can also be restricted to narrow terminals so it doesn't duplicate the sidebar.
